title: Definite Integral Substitutions and the Area Between Curves
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Substitution in Definite Integrals
definitions.statement: When performing a substitution u = g(x) on a definite integral, the limits of integration change from x = a and x = b to u = g(a) and u = g(b), eliminating the need to back-substitute.
conditions: f is continuous on range of g
definitions.explanation: Evaluating at transformed limits saves algebraic steps and prevents domain errors.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Always transform limits when substituting in definite integrals.

definitions.title: Area Between Intersecting Curves
definitions.latex: A = \int_a^b [f(x) - g(x)] dx, \quad \text{where } f(x) \ge g(x) \; \forall x \in [a, b]
definitions.statement: The area of the region bounded by continuous curves y = f(x) and y = g(x) between x = a and x = b equals the integral of the upper curve minus the lower curve.
definitions.explanation: If curves intersect and switch positions, the total area is int_a^b |f(x) - g(x)| dx.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Area equals integral of (Top Curve - Bottom Curve) dx or (Right Curve - Left Curve) dy.
